parsed.why: No trans-specific offence and paper protections with an equality body that acts, but extreme social rejection (79% reject neighbours), hate speech unpunished, past Pride attacks and police refusing to investigate anti-LGBT arson; bank service denial documented. Not criminalised, but recourse thin.

Same-sex conduct criminalised and enforced (2023 arrests, 1–2 year sentences), president's public call to stone, no legal recognition, no protection, arbitrary detention and torture in a state of general repression. Outed trans visitor faces custody and severe harm.

Cross-dressing and same-sex relations legal, strong institutional protections and court relief, convictions upheld for assaulting trans tourists, healthcare funded. Remaining drags: no nationwide trans-specific service protection, continued transphobic violence, regional pockets of hostility.

No criminalisation, but no hate-crime or gender-identity protection and documented police raid on an LGBT venue detaining ~30, extortion and a baseless 'homosexuality' charge; no working document route for trans visitors; persecution tracking political crisis.

Robust legal protection, aggravation for transphobic crime, funded care, but documented visitor-facing border questioning, a hostel dorm dispute, 64% of trans respondents reporting discrimination, and persistent birth-sex prison placement with isolation and strip-search exposure under official findings.
